column1: text
Whoever you are, I hope your shoes are comfortable. Mine were not.
There was a pigeon earlier that looked at me like it knew something. Keep an eye out.
I ate my emergency snack at minute nine. Learn from me.
If the person behind you is humming, it's fine. They were behind me too.
I don't know you but I'm proud of you for standing here.
Somebody's phone alarm has been going off in a bag for twenty minutes. Nobody has claimed it.
Check your pockets. You have more receipts than you think.
I counted the windows on the building across the street. There are 41. Now you don't have to.
My mum texted 'are you still in that line' and I said yes and she said 'ok' and that was the whole conversation.
It's going to rain in a minute. Or it was, when I wrote this. Either way, hi.
Don't lean on the post. It moves.
I had a whole speech planned for this and now it's just: good luck with the rest of your day.
Someone ahead of me was wearing two different shoes. On purpose, I think. Iconic.
You've waited longer than you think. That's the thing about it.
I'd tell you what I'm having for dinner but I don't know yet either.
There's a bakery two streets over. Don't go. But it's there.
I've been thinking about a song for an hour and I still don't know what it's called.
Nobody's going to ask, so: how are you, actually?
If you're reading this, someone stood exactly here and thought about you. That's all. That's the message.
Standing still for this long makes you realise how much you usually move.
I came here after work and now I'm not sure which one was the job.
I hope the weather's the same as when I left. It was pretty good.
The person in front of me was called Dev and he never said a word. Dev, if this is you, hi.
I did not need to be here. I stayed anyway. That felt important to say.
There's a vending machine on the corner and it only sells one thing and I still don't know what it is.
My step count is huge. My steps were all in place.
Nothing happened while I waited and it was the best afternoon I've had in weeks.
Tell the next person something kind. I'm telling you: you're doing great.
I met a stranger here who's now a person I'll think about occasionally forever.
At one point everyone in the line looked up at the same time. I don't know why. Nothing was there.
I made a list of things I'd do after this. I lost the list. I feel free.
Somebody offered me half a sandwich. I said no and I regret it, and I'll regret it for years.
The line moved twice while I wasn't looking and both times I felt like I'd missed something.
I brought a book and read the same page four times. Good page.
The awning drips. Stand slightly to the left.
I'm writing this with cold hands. If it's warm where you are, enjoy it for me.
The kid in front of me asked their dad what we were waiting for and he said 'you'll see' and I've been thinking about it since.
Whatever you write next, make it better than this. It's not hard.
I don't have advice. I have this: you're nearly there. That's a fact, not encouragement.
My coffee's gone cold. It was cold when I got it. Something to think about.
There's a sock on the pavement near the bins. It's been there the whole time. It might be there for you too.
I texted 'nearly there' to three people and it was never true until now.
If you see someone in a yellow raincoat, they were nice to me. Be nice to them.
I wanted to say something profound. I'm hungry. That's what I've got.
You'll forget most of this wait. I'm hoping you don't forget this bit.
Somebody behind me is explaining the offside rule to nobody. It's been going on for a while.
I got here early. It didn't matter. Nothing about getting here early mattered. I loved it anyway.
Please don't tap the door. Someone did and we all felt it.
I've been here so long my phone thinks this is my home.
Hello from earlier. It's later now. That's the whole trick.
